Bodkin is a sniper terminal for pons v2 on Robinhood Chain. Here is everything it does.

It reads a launch the second it lands. Dev buy, creator tax, who collects the fees, how many wallets are exempt from the opening tax, what the deployer shipped before.

Then it scores that launch from 0 to 100 and prints the reason next to the number, so you can argue with it.

Every rule behind that number is yours to edit. Dev share, tax ceiling, minimum score, take profit, stop, trailing, max hold.

The opening tax starts at 99 percent and decays to 0 in three seconds.

Bodkin does not race it. It polls the tax for your own address every 150 ms and buys the moment it drops under your ceiling.

The launch of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra marks a clear transition in AI capabilities: moving from copilot assistance (generating text and code) towards direct computer control (executing multi-step workflows across applications, terminals, and browsers).  

While the technical jump is substantial, deployment remains gated under enterprise admin controls and access restrictions; meaning adoption will be measured, not overnight.  

Investment Implications: 

Legacy SaaS (Value Compression): Seat-based SaaS pricing faces structural pressure as agents execute workflows that previously required individual user seats. Mid-tier apps acting primarily as thin GUIs risk being reduced to low-margin systems of record.  

Inference & Power (Structural Demand): Multi-step, agentic execution increases token volume and compute per completed job relative to single-prompt queries. This sustains high capital intensity across compute, networking and energy infrastructure.  

Context & Governance Holders (Durable Moats): Models require live operational context to act safely. Value and pricing power accrue to platforms that control proprietary enterprise data, identity, permissions and audit logs.  

Bottom Line: Value is likely to shift away from thin middle-layer application software, concentrating instead in underlying compute and power infrastructure and in the platform layers governing enterprise execution.

This is Mutt, a French Bulldog who served with the YMCA's Cigarette Dog delivery service during WWI. His job was simple but dangerous: carry cigarettes to soldiers on the front lines with the 11th Engineers. He was wounded twice in the line of duty but kept working. When the engineers shipped home at war's end, mascots were normally left behind but the men refused to leave Mutt in France.

They smuggled him aboard, and he made it home to New York.

Beldex: The Whole Privacy Stack
here's what kills me about the privacy space in 2026:

everyone's still building single apps. one coin for payments. one VPN. one messenger. one browser.

meanwhile, surveillance isn't single-app. it's a stack. your ISP sees what you browse. apps see what you message. chains see what you transact. identity layers leak across all of it.

you can't beat a stack with a tool.

that's what makes @BeldexCoin different. they didn't build a privacy coin. they built a privacy operating system:

 BChat : end-to-end encrypted messaging, no phone number tied to identity

 BelNet : decentralized VPN routing traffic through node operators

 Beldex Browser : private browsing baked in at the protocol level

 Beldex DEX : private swaps, no KYC, no address history

 BDX : the value layer connecting all of it, with ring signatures + stealth addresses for transaction privacy

every layer talks to the others. your identity doesn't leak between apps because the apps were never separate apps to begin with.

most "ecosystems" are a token + a roadmap slide. beldex has shipped four production products used by hundreds of thousands of people. that's the difference between a privacy narrative and privacy infrastructure.

the thesis is simple: privacy isn't a feature you bolt on. it's the default you build around.

if you're still picking which single layer of your life to protect, you're already losing. the surveillance machine is integrated. your defense should be too.

$BDX isn't competing with monero. it's competing with the entire extractive web.

start with one product. you'll end up needing all of them.

THE SPACE INDUSTRY THIS WEEK

The 20 biggest stories and developments shaping the space industry this week, all in one place, ranked by Impact:
_____
1/20 - $PL: Planet delivered record quarterly revenue of $116.1 million, up 58% year over year, with $13.9 million in adjusted EBITDA, $814.9 million in backlog and $865.4 million in liquidity.

Full-year revenue guidance reached $430–441 million.
_____
2/20 - NASA awarded Blue Origin a firm-fixed-price contract worth up to $700 million to deliver and operate a Mars telecommunications orbiter.

$RDW: Redwire supplies Blue Ring hardware, including ROSA wings, power distribution units and cameras. 
_____
3/20 - OHB signed a contract worth nearly €1 billion with SES to develop and produce 18 medium Earth orbit (MEO) satellite platforms for Europe’s IRIS² secure-connectivity network.

This is the program’s first major manufacturing award and a production-scale commitment to sovereign European connectivity.
_____
4/20 - $RKLB: Rocket Lab passed preliminary design review for the 18 missile-warning satellites it is building for the Space Development Agency.

The milestone reduces execution risk on the existing $816 million Tracking Layer Tranche 3 program.
_____
5/20 - $SPCX: The Department of War deployed Starshield AI’s Grok for Government across its secure GenAImil environment.

The system is accredited for controlled unclassified information at Impact Level 5, while the platform has onboarded more than 1.7 million users.
_____
6/20 - $SPCX: SpaceX and 4iG Group signed Europe’s first combined Starlink Mobile and sovereign-satellite agreement.

Initial service targets Hungary and Albania, followed by next-generation coverage across those markets, Montenegro and North Macedonia.
_____
7/20 - $LUNR: Intuitive Machines booked an order for two IM 300 spacecraft from a new, undisclosed customer.

The award opens a new customer segment and extends the platform beyond its existing mission base. 
_____
8/20 - Sierra Space secured national-security and commercial payload contracts for Dream Chaser’s inaugural orbital mission.
_____
9/20 - Galactic Energy successfully completed the maiden orbital flight of its Pallas-1 liquid-fueled rocket.

The vehicle reached its intended orbit and completed the stated test objectives, giving China’s commercial launch sector another medium-lift platform. 
_____
10/20 - $PL: Planet signed a seven-figure, one-year agreement with a European defense and intelligence customer.

The customer will use Planet’s intelligence across critical areas for operational planning.
_____
11/20 - $SATL: Satellogic made SynMax the exclusive maritime-intelligence channel for its planned Merlin constellation.

Merlin is designed to combine daily, one meter class imagery with vessel identification data for dark-vessel detection, sanctions monitoring and illegal-fishing analysis. Its first launch is planned for October.
_____
12/20 - AEye won a multi-million-dollar contract to supply Apollo lidar for Lunar Outpost’s Pegasus lunar vehicle.

The sensors will support terrain perception, obstacle detection and autonomous navigation, marking AEye’s first commercial move into lunar mobility.
_____
13/20 - $YSS: York Space Systems introduced LX/V-CLASS, a spacecraft platform designed specifically for sustained operations in very low Earth orbit (VLEO).
_____
14/20 - $RKLB: Rocket Lab completed Electron’s 94th mission and its 15th launch of 2026, deploying Synspective’s 11th StriX radar imaging satellite.

Sixteen additional dedicated Synspective missions are contracted before 2030.
_____
15/20 - $VOYG: Voyager Technologies detailed its lunar platform, including a dedicated lunar-systems team and three planned Moon landings.
_____
16/20 - Northwood opened a 185,000-square-foot headquarters and factory to mass-produce satellite ground infrastructure.

Manufacturing space will expand from 25,000 to 135,000 square feet, production is scheduled to move in October and 400 jobs are planned over three years.
_____
17/20 - Sceye and SoftBank completed a 15,000-kilometer stratospheric connectivity mission from New Mexico to Japan.

The aircraft connected ordinary phones, communicated with drones and demonstrated onboard edge computing with 68-millisecond response times, more than 40% faster than cloud processing in the test.
_____
18/20 - India successfully launched EOS-05 into its intended orbit aboard GSLV-F17.

The mission delivered India’s first Earth imaging satellite designed for geosynchronous orbit, expanding potential persistent regional observation capacity. 
_____
19/20 - $PL: Planet shipped Tanager-2 and 18 SuperDoves to Vandenberg ahead of SpaceX’s Transporter-18 mission.

Tanager-2 is intended to expand hyperspectral capacity, while the SuperDoves will replenish Planet’s daily global-imaging constellation.
_____
20/20 - Katalyst Space advanced its LINK servicing demonstration near NASA’s Swift telescope but an Attitude-control problems prevented the planned boost, and no closer approach will occur.

LINK deployed three robotic arms, fired all three electric thrusters and approached within 12–15 kilometers of Swift.
